info.name: Orichal API
info.description:
The API of Orichal, a simulated crypto exchange (CE-2), from the server in `server/`.

Choose the environment **Orichal local** and run the folders top to bottom on a freshly seeded database. Scripts save the tokens and ids in the environment, and the next requests read them from there. Every answer is checked for the envelope by the collection's own script; each request adds its status and the fields that matter.

`npm run test:api` runs the same collection with Newman, on a server and a MongoDB of its own.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Register, refresh, log out and in again; the 2FA step; the lockout.

The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie (`rt`), which Postman keeps in its cookie jar by itself. A login ends the earlier session of the same browser, found through that cookie. Postman has one jar, so the trader's and the admin's logins have "Disable cookie jar" on: each is a browser of its own.

request.description: Reaching findOne, it would match any user.
One character more: the signature doesn't match.
Mongoose can't cast the text to an ObjectId and throws a CastError; errorHandler answers 404, because nothing has that id.

request.description: It exists, but not for this user. A 403 would say that it exists.
The unique index on users.email refuses the insert with E11000; Mongoose's post-save middleware (schemas/User.js) turns it into this 409.
Well made, but the market's rules refuse it: the engine answers, not Zod.
